chunks: Design an arbiter and compare types. The question: Design an arbiter. What are the different types and their tradeoffs?
An arbiter is a small circuit that decides who gets to use something shared when several users ask at the same moment, such as a memory port or a bus (shared data wires).
It lets exactly one requester through at a time. The key design choice is the policy. Fixed priority always favors the same requester.
Round-robin takes turns, so everyone is served eventually.
Picture a meeting with one microphone. With fixed priority, the boss always speaks first, and a junior colleague may never get a turn if the boss keeps talking.
With round-robin, the microphone is passed around the table, so each person waits for at most everyone else to speak once.
The meeting picture leaves out hardware timing: the decision must be made within one clock cycle.
Fixed priority with all three requesters asserting continuously: requester 0 takes every grant, requesters 1 and 2 starve.
Priority is the correct design when a requester's importance is absolute, but it is dangerous for shared bandwidth.
Request / grant: a requester raises request, and the arbiter raises grant for one winner. Starvation: a requester that is never granted because others always win.
Fixed priority: requester 0 beats 1, which beats 2, and so on. Round-robin: priority rotates so the most recent winner goes to the back of the line.
One-hot: a signal with exactly one bit set, such as grant 0010.
Four requesters all ask every cycle. A fixed-priority arbiter grants requester 0 every time, and the others starve. A round-robin arbiter grants 0, 1, 2, 3, 0, 1, and so on.
For fixed priority, a neat trick finds the winner: if the request bits are 1010 (requesters 1 and 3 asking), then req & -req gives 0010, which keeps only the lowest set bit.
With round-robin, a requester waits for at most the other N-1 grants. That is the whole idea.
"An arbiter picks one winner among simultaneous requests. Fixed priority is a priority encoder, req & -req , tiny and fast but it can starve low-priority requesters.
Round-robin keeps a mask or pointer so every requester gets a turn, with a worst-case wait of N minus 1 grants.
Other schemes are weighted round-robin, matrix or LRU, age-based and time-division, each trading fairness and latency guarantees against area and timing."
Quick check. Which expression isolates the lowest set bit of the request vector r ?
